builtinCredentialProviders.$comment: Credential providers built into Cargo (`BUILT_IN_PROVIDERS`). The `cargo:` prefix is reserved for these; any other `cargo:` name is executed as a program of that literal name. alias.title: [alias]
alias.description:
Cargo command aliases. Each key is a subcommand name; the value is the command to run, either a single string (split on whitespace) or an array of arguments. Aliases are recursive and may not redefine existing built-in Cargo commands. Per-alias values can also be set via the `CARGO_ALIAS_<name>` environment variable.

The value continues the `cargo` command line, so it must not repeat `cargo` itself: write `run --release`, not `cargo run --release`.

Aliases may also be grouped into subtables: `[alias] my.foo = "check"` defines `cargo my.foo`, since Cargo addresses an alias by its configuration path.

[Cargo documentation](https://doc.rust-lang.org/cargo/reference/config.html#alias)

docs.main:
Defines [Cargo command aliases](https://doc.rust-lang.org/cargo/reference/config.html#alias).

Each key is the subcommand name and the value is what `cargo <key>` expands to. Use a string (split on whitespace) or an array (preserves whitespace inside arguments).

**Built-in aliases** (may be overridden): `b` → `build`, `c` → `check`, `d` → `doc`, `t` → `test`, `r` → `run`, `rm` → `remove`.

Aliases are recursive — one alias may invoke another. Aliases may **not** redefine existing built-in Cargo commands.

The value continues the command line after `cargo`, so it must not start with `cargo` or `cargo-<name>`, with an option, or with a `+toolchain` directive.

Each alias may also be set via the `CARGO_ALIAS_<name>` environment variable.

aliasCommandArray.title: argument list
aliasCommandArray.description: Subcommand followed by arguments, passed through verbatim. Use this form to preserve arguments containing spaces.

prefixItems.description: Subcommand the alias expands to: a single token, with no embedded whitespace.

allOf.$comment: The expansion is appended to `cargo`, so a leading `cargo` produces `cargo cargo ...` and fails with a `no such command` error. A leading `cargo-<name>` fails the same way, because Cargo resolves external subcommands by searching for `cargo-cargo-<name>`.

The expansion must start with a subcommand. A leading option fails with `unexpected argument`, and a leading `+toolchain` fails with `no such command`, since rustup, not Cargo, resolves toolchain directives.

aliasCommandString.title: command string
aliasCommandString.description: Subcommand and arguments, split on whitespace.

allOf.$comment: The expansion is appended to `cargo`, so a leading `cargo` produces `cargo cargo ...` and fails with a `no such command` error. A leading `cargo-<name>` fails the same way, because Cargo resolves external subcommands by searching for `cargo-cargo-<name>`.

The expansion must start with a subcommand. A leading option fails with `unexpected argument`, and a leading `+toolchain` fails with `no such command`, since rustup, not Cargo, resolves toolchain directives.

aliasName.$comment: Cargo builds the lookup key by splitting on `.`, so a key containing a dot is unreachable: `"my.foo" = "check"` can never be invoked, while the subtable form `my.foo = "check"` defines `cargo my.foo`. Every other name is reachable, including names with whitespace and names starting with `-` or `+`, which are invocable as `cargo -- -x` (verified against cargo 1.98.1), so they are not restricted here.
aliasName.description: Cargo subcommand name, or one dot-separated segment of one. Any string without a `.`; a dot is the configuration path separator, so use a subtable to define `cargo <a>.<b>`.

aliasNode1.$comment: An alias entry: the command it expands to, or a subtable of further name segments. Nesting is unrolled to 6 levels (aliasNode1..aliasNode6) rather than written as a recursive $ref, because Tombi stops following a cyclic $ref after one level and would reject a valid `a.b.c` alias. Cargo itself imposes no depth limit; an alias nested more than 6 deep is accepted by Cargo and rejected here.

oneOf.title: alias name segments
oneOf.description: Subtable grouping further alias name segments. Cargo addresses an alias by configuration path and joins the segments with dots, so `[alias] my.foo = "check"` defines `cargo my.foo`.

aliasNode6.$comment: Deepest unrolled level: leaves only, so nesting stops at 6 segments.

builtinCommands.$comment: Built-in Cargo commands (`commands::builtin_exec`). An alias with one of these names is discarded at startup with `user-defined alias <name> is ignored, because it is shadowed by a built-in command`. The built-in aliases `b`, `c`, `d`, `t`, `r` and `rm` are deliberately absent: a user alias takes precedence over those. Referenced from `propertyNames` under `not`.

cargoInvocationToken.$comment: A first token that names the `cargo` binary (bare, `.exe`-suffixed or path-qualified) or a `cargo-<name>` subcommand binary. `cargofmt` and other tokens that merely begin with the letters `cargo` are not matched, since those are legitimate alias or subcommand names.

toolchainOrOptionToken.$comment: A first token starting with `-` (parsed as an unexpected argument, since the subcommand must come first) or `+` (a rustup toolchain directive that Cargo itself cannot resolve).

warnings.description:
Adjust the effective level of lint warnings for local packages. MSRV: respected as of Rust 1.97.

[Cargo documentation](https://doc.rust-lang.org/cargo/reference/config.html#buildwarnings)

enumValues: Continue to emit the lints as warnings (default).
Emit an error for a crate that has lint warnings. Use `--keep-going` to see the lint warnings for all dependent crates.

deny.description: Emit an error for a crate that has lint warnings.

warn.description: Continue to emit the lints as warnings (default).

jobs.description:
Maximum number of compiler processes to run in parallel. Negative values are relative to the number of logical CPUs. The string "default" resets to Cargo defaults. Defaults to the number of logical CPUs.

[Cargo documentation](https://doc.rust-lang.org/cargo/reference/config.html#buildjobs)

rustc-wrapper.description:
Wrapper executable to run instead of rustc. The first argument passed to the wrapper is the path to the actual rustc executable.
https://doc.rust-lang.org/cargo/reference/config.html#buildrustc-wrapper An empty string disables the wrapper.

rustc-workspace-wrapper.description:
Wrapper executable to run instead of rustc for workspace members only. If both rustc-wrapper and rustc-workspace-wrapper are set, invocations are nested: $RUSTC_WRAPPER $RUSTC_WORKSPACE_WRAPPER $RUSTC.
https://doc.rust-lang.org/cargo/reference/config.html#buildrustc-workspace-wrapper An empty string disables the wrapper.

target.description:
Default target platform triple, custom target spec path, "host-tuple", or list of targets. Defaults to the host platform when unset.

[Cargo documentation](https://doc.rust-lang.org/cargo/reference/config.html#buildtarget)

target-dir.description:
Directory where all compiler output is placed. Defaults to a directory named `target` at the workspace root.

[Cargo documentation](https://doc.rust-lang.org/cargo/reference/config.html#buildtarget-dir)

build-dir.description:
Directory where intermediate build artifacts are stored. Defaults to the value of `build.target-dir`. Supports path templating with `{workspace-root}`, `{cargo-cache-home}`, and `{workspace-path-hash}`.

[Cargo documentation](https://doc.rust-lang.org/cargo/reference/config.html#buildbuild-dir)

rustflags.description:
Extra command-line flags passed to rustc. May be an array of strings or a space-separated string.

[Cargo documentation](https://doc.rust-lang.org/cargo/reference/config.html#buildrustflags)

rustdocflags.description:
Extra command-line flags passed to rustdoc. May be an array of strings or a space-separated string.

[Cargo documentation](https://doc.rust-lang.org/cargo/reference/config.html#buildrustdocflags)

incremental.description:
Whether to enable incremental compilation. When unset, the value from the active profile is used; when set, this overrides every profile.

[Cargo documentation](https://doc.rust-lang.org/cargo/reference/config.html#buildincremental)

dep-info-basedir.description:
Config-relative path prefix stripped from dep-info file paths, used to convert absolute paths to relative paths for downstream tools.

[Cargo documentation](https://doc.rust-lang.org/cargo/reference/config.html#builddep-info-basedir)

pipelining.description:
DEPRECATED. This option is unused. Cargo always has pipelining enabled.

[Cargo documentation](https://doc.rust-lang.org/cargo/reference/config.html#buildpipelining)

artifact-dir.description: UNSTABLE: Copy final artifacts to this directory; requires -Z unstable-options.

sbom.description: UNSTABLE: Generate SBOM precursor files; requires -Z sbom.

fingerprint.description: UNSTABLE: Freshness comparison method; requires -Z checksum-freshness.

analysis.description: UNSTABLE: Persist build metrics; requires -Z build-analysis.

auto-clean-frequency.description:
How often Cargo checks whether unused global cache files should be deleted. Accepts "never", "always", or an integer followed by "seconds", "minutes", "hours", "days", "weeks", or "months" (e.g. "1 day", "2 weeks").

[Cargo documentation](https://doc.rust-lang.org/cargo/reference/config.html#cacheauto-clean-frequency)

docs.main:
How often Cargo checks whether unused global cache files should be deleted.

Accepts:
- `"never"` --- never delete old files.
- `"always"` --- check on every Cargo run.
- `<integer> <unit>` where unit is one of `seconds`, `minutes`, `hours`, `days`, `weeks`, or `months` (e.g. `"1 day"`, `"2 weeks"`).

Default: `"1 day"`. Environment: `CARGO_CACHE_AUTO_CLEAN_FREQUENCY`.

global-clean.description: UNSTABLE: Global cache retention; requires -Z gc.

vcs.description:
Source control system used when initializing a new repository.
Defaults to `git`, or `none` when run inside an existing VCS repository. Overridable via `cargo new --vcs`.
Environment: `CARGO_CARGO_NEW_VCS`.

[Cargo documentation](https://doc.rust-lang.org/cargo/reference/config.html#cargo-newvcs)

enumValues: Do not initialize any VCS repository (also the implicit default when nested inside an existing repo).

none.description: Do not initialize any VCS repository (also the implicit default when nested inside an existing repo).

additionalProperties.title: credential provider command
additionalProperties.description:
Credential provider command for this alias: an executable path with optional arguments. Reference the alias name from `registry.global-credential-providers` or `registries.<NAME>.credential-provider`.

[Cargo documentation](https://doc.rust-lang.org/cargo/reference/config.html#credential-alias)

oneOf.title: command string
oneOf.description: Path and arguments, split on spaces.

oneOf.title: path and arguments
oneOf.description: Executable path followed by arguments, passed through verbatim. Use this form for a path or argument containing spaces.

prefixItems.description: Path to the credential provider executable, or the name of a built-in `cargo:` provider.

propertyNames.$comment: No shape restriction: `registries.<NAME>.credential-provider` splits a string reference on spaces, but the array form passes the first element verbatim and `ConfigKey::from_parts` does not split it, so `credential-provider = ["my alias"]` reaches an alias named `my alias`.
propertyNames.description: Alias name, as referenced from `registry.global-credential-providers` or `registries.<NAME>.credential-provider`. A name containing whitespace is only reachable through the array form of those references. Names of built-in providers are rejected because Cargo ignores aliases that shadow them.

browser.description:
Browser command used by cargo doc --open, overriding the BROWSER environment variable. Either a single program path or an array of [program, ...args].

[Cargo documentation](https://doc.rust-lang.org/cargo/reference/config.html#docbrowser)

extern-map.description: UNSTABLE: External rustdoc links; requires -Z rustdoc-map.

env.title: [env]
env.description:
Environment variables set for build scripts, rustc invocations, cargo run, and cargo build.

[Cargo documentation](https://doc.rust-lang.org/cargo/reference/config.html#env)

envEntry.title: env entry
envEntry.description:
Value for an environment variable injected into build scripts, rustc, `cargo run`, and `cargo build`. Either a bare string or an inline table that opts into `force` (override an existing env var) or `relative` (resolve `value` relative to the config file's directory).

[Cargo documentation](https://doc.rust-lang.org/cargo/reference/config.html#env)

oneOf.title: literal value
oneOf.description: Literal string assigned to the environment variable.

oneOf.title: expanded value
oneOf.description: Inline table form. Required: `value`. Optional flags: `force`, `relative`.

value.title: variable value
value.description: String exported as the variable's value. When `relative = true`, this is interpreted as a path relative to the parent directory of the `.cargo/` directory containing this config file, and the exported value is the resolved absolute path.

force.title: force
force.description: When `true`, override the variable even if it is already present in the parent environment. Defaults to `false` (existing values win).

relative.title: relative
relative.description: When `true`, treat `value` as a path relative to the parent directory of the `.cargo/` directory containing this config file. Cargo resolves it to an absolute path before exporting. Defaults to `false`.

docs.main:
Environment variable value.

Use a bare string for a literal value, or an inline table to opt into:

- `force = true` — override an existing variable in the parent environment (default leaves it untouched).
- `relative = true` — resolve `value` as a path relative to the parent directory of the `.cargo/` directory containing this config file; the exported variable holds the resulting absolute path.

[Cargo reference](https://doc.rust-lang.org/cargo/reference/config.html#env)

frequency.description:
How often Cargo displays future incompatibility report notifications.

[Cargo documentation](https://doc.rust-lang.org/cargo/reference/config.html#future-incompat-reportfrequency)

docs.main:
Controls how often Cargo displays a notification to the terminal when a future incompat report is available.

Possible values:
- `"always"` --- always display a notification when a command (e.g. `cargo build`) produces a future incompat report.
- `"never"` --- never display a notification.

Default: `"always"`. Environment: `CARGO_FUTURE_INCOMPAT_REPORT_FREQUENCY`.

http.title: [http]
http.description:
HTTP behavior for fetching crates and accessing remote git repositories.

[Cargo documentation](https://doc.rust-lang.org/cargo/reference/config.html#http)

debug.description:
Enable HTTP debugging. Combine with `CARGO_LOG=network=debug` (or `network=trace`) to see request details. Logs may contain authentication tokens, do not share publicly.

[Cargo documentation](https://doc.rust-lang.org/cargo/reference/config.html#httpdebug)

proxy.description:
HTTP and HTTPS proxy in libcurl format `[protocol://]host[:port]`. Falls back to git's `http.proxy`, then to `HTTPS_PROXY`/`https_proxy`/`http_proxy` env vars.
https://doc.rust-lang.org/cargo/reference/config.html#httpproxy An empty string disables proxy use.

timeout.description:
Timeout for each HTTP request, in seconds.

[Cargo documentation](https://doc.rust-lang.org/cargo/reference/config.html#httptimeout)

cainfo.description:
Path to a Certificate Authority (CA) bundle file used to verify TLS certificates. If unset, Cargo uses the system trust store.

[Cargo documentation](https://doc.rust-lang.org/cargo/reference/config.html#httpcainfo)

proxy-cainfo.description:
Path to a Certificate Authority (CA) bundle file used to verify proxy TLS certificates. Falls back to `http.cainfo` if unset.

[Cargo documentation](https://doc.rust-lang.org/cargo/reference/config.html#httpproxy-cainfo)

check-revoke.description:
Whether TLS certificate revocation checks are performed. Only works on Windows. Default: `true` on Windows, `false` elsewhere.

[Cargo documentation](https://doc.rust-lang.org/cargo/reference/config.html#httpcheck-revoke)

ssl-version.description:
Minimum TLS version, or a table with `min`/`max` TLS version bounds. Cargo's default range is `min = "tlsv1.0"`, `max` = newest supported (typically `tlsv1.3`).

[Cargo documentation](https://doc.rust-lang.org/cargo/reference/config.html#httpssl-version)

low-speed-limit.description:
Average transfer speed threshold, in bytes per second. If the transfer rate stays below this for `http.timeout` seconds, Cargo aborts and retries.

[Cargo documentation](https://doc.rust-lang.org/cargo/reference/config.html#httplow-speed-limit)

multiplexing.description:
Whether Cargo attempts to use HTTP/2 with multiplexing. If `false`, falls back to HTTP/1.1 without pipelining.

[Cargo documentation](https://doc.rust-lang.org/cargo/reference/config.html#httpmultiplexing)

user-agent.description:
Custom HTTP user-agent header. Default is a string including Cargo's version.

[Cargo documentation](https://doc.rust-lang.org/cargo/reference/config.html#httpuser-agent)

oneOf.title: Minimum TLS version
oneOf.description: Minimum TLS version to use; cargo accepts any newer version up to the platform maximum.

enumValues: System-default TLS version selection (cargo's built-in defaults: min `tlsv1.0`, max newest supported).
TLS 1.x family (system-chosen minor version). Prefer an explicit `tlsv1.2` or `tlsv1.3`.

default.description: System-default TLS version selection (cargo's built-in defaults: min `tlsv1.0`, max newest supported).

tlsv1.description: TLS 1.x family (system-chosen minor version). Prefer an explicit `tlsv1.2` or `tlsv1.3`.

root.description:
Root directory for installed executables. Executables go into a `bin` directory underneath the root, alongside tracking files `.crates.toml` and `.crates2.json`. Defaults to Cargo's home directory (typically `~/.cargo`). Overridable with `--root` or `CARGO_INSTALL_ROOT`.

[Cargo documentation](https://doc.rust-lang.org/cargo/reference/config.html#installroot)

retry.description:
Number of times to retry possibly spurious network errors.

[Cargo documentation](https://doc.rust-lang.org/cargo/reference/config.html#netretry)

git-fetch-with-cli.description:
Use the git executable for fetching registry indexes and git dependencies.

[Cargo documentation](https://doc.rust-lang.org/cargo/reference/config.html#netgit-fetch-with-cli)

offline.description:
Avoid accessing the network and use locally cached data where possible.

[Cargo documentation](https://doc.rust-lang.org/cargo/reference/config.html#netoffline)

known-hosts.description:
SSH host keys accepted by Cargo.

[Cargo documentation](https://doc.rust-lang.org/cargo/reference/config.html#netsshknown-hosts)

patch.title: [patch]
patch.description:
Dependency patch overrides. Outer key is the registry name being patched (typically `crates-io`, or a name from `[registries]`); inner key is the package name being replaced; innermost table is the replacement dependency specification, using the same format as Cargo.toml `[patch]`.

[Cargo documentation](https://doc.rust-lang.org/cargo/reference/config.html#patch)

additionalProperties.description:
Patches keyed by registry name. The conventional key is `crates-io`; user-defined registry names from `[registries]` are also valid.

[Cargo documentation](https://doc.rust-lang.org/cargo/reference/overriding-dependencies.html#the-patch-section)

dep-spec.description: Replacement dependency: version string or dependency table. Cargo validates source conflicts and resolves the replacement crate.

version.description:
Semver requirement matched against the patched package.

[Cargo documentation](https://doc.rust-lang.org/cargo/reference/specifying-dependencies.html)

path.description:
Filesystem path to the replacement crate. Relative paths resolve relative to the config file containing this `[patch]` section.

[Cargo documentation](https://doc.rust-lang.org/cargo/reference/config.html#patch)

git.description:
Git repository URL providing the replacement crate.

[Cargo documentation](https://doc.rust-lang.org/cargo/reference/specifying-dependencies.html#specifying-dependencies-from-git-repositories)

branch.description: Git branch to use. Mutually exclusive with `tag` and `rev`.

tag.description: Git tag to use. Mutually exclusive with `branch` and `rev`.

rev.description: Git revision (commit-ish) to use. Mutually exclusive with `branch` and `tag`.

package.description:
Real package name when the patch entry's key is a rename. Lets you patch a crate while referring to it under a different name in your manifest.

[Cargo documentation](https://doc.rust-lang.org/cargo/reference/specifying-dependencies.html#renaming-dependencies-in-cargotoml)

registry.description: Name of the registry the replacement is fetched from when using `version`. Refers to a key under `[registries]`.

default-features.description: Parsed but ignored for patch selection; configure features on the dependency that uses this patch.

features.description: Parsed but ignored for patch selection; configure features on the dependency that uses this patch.

optional.description: Whether the dependency is optional. Rarely meaningful inside `[patch]`; included for parity with the dependency-table format.

public.description: Whether the dependency is part of the public API (unstable nightly feature).

registry-index.description: Internal registry index URL used by Cargo when publishing.

base.description: UNSTABLE: Named path base; requires path-bases support.

lib.description: UNSTABLE: Also use the artifact dependency as a library; requires -Z bindeps.

target.description: UNSTABLE: Artifact target platform; requires -Z bindeps.

profiles.title: [profile.*]
profiles.description:
Profile configuration overlays workspace/manifest profiles. Custom profiles require inherits after merging, but a configuration overlay may omit it.

[Cargo source](https://github.com/rust-lang/cargo/blob/cc5596f058e623d22be718adf541a9bd766d9417/src/workspace/profiles.rs)

dev.description:
Built-in `dev` profile (used by `cargo build` and `cargo run`).
Defaults: `opt-level = 0`, `debug = true`, `debug-assertions = true`, `overflow-checks = true`, `lto = false`, `panic = "unwind"`, `incremental = true`, `codegen-units = 256`, `rpath = false`.

[Cargo documentation](https://doc.rust-lang.org/cargo/reference/profiles.html#dev)

release.description:
Built-in `release` profile (used by `cargo build --release`, `cargo install`).
Defaults: `opt-level = 3`, `debug = false`, `debug-assertions = false`, `overflow-checks = false`, `lto = false`, `panic = "unwind"`, `incremental = false`, `codegen-units = 16`, `rpath = false`.

[Cargo documentation](https://doc.rust-lang.org/cargo/reference/profiles.html#release)

test.description:
Built-in `test` profile (used by `cargo test`). Inherits from `dev`.

[Cargo documentation](https://doc.rust-lang.org/cargo/reference/profiles.html#test)

bench.description:
Built-in `bench` profile (used by `cargo bench`). Inherits from `release`.

[Cargo documentation](https://doc.rust-lang.org/cargo/reference/profiles.html#bench)

propertyNames.description: Cargo profile name: Unicode letters/numbers, underscore or hyphen; Cargo checks reserved names.

buildOverride.description:
Override profile settings for build scripts, proc-macros, and their dependencies. Accepts the same keys as a normal profile (excluding nested `package` and `build-override`).

[Cargo documentation](https://doc.rust-lang.org/cargo/reference/profiles.html#overrides)

rustflags.description: UNSTABLE: Extra compiler flags; requires -Z profile-rustflags.

codegen-backend.description: UNSTABLE: Compiler codegen backend; requires -Z codegen-backend.

trim-paths.description: UNSTABLE: Trim filesystem paths; requires -Z trim-paths.

hint-mostly-unused.description: UNSTABLE: Mark crates mostly unused; requires -Z profile-hint-mostly-unused.

dir-name.description: Removed: directory names follow the profile name.

builtinProfile.description:
Settings for one of the four built-in Cargo profiles. Cargo errors out if `inherits` is set on a built-in profile.

[Cargo documentation](https://doc.rust-lang.org/cargo/reference/profiles.html)

rustflags.description: UNSTABLE: Extra compiler flags; requires -Z profile-rustflags.

codegen-backend.description: UNSTABLE: Compiler codegen backend; requires -Z codegen-backend.

trim-paths.description: UNSTABLE: Trim filesystem paths; requires -Z trim-paths.

hint-mostly-unused.description: UNSTABLE: Mark crates mostly unused; requires -Z profile-hint-mostly-unused.

dir-name.description: Removed: directory names follow the profile name.

codegenUnits.title: codegen-units
codegenUnits.description: Number of parallel code generation units per crate. Defaults depend on incremental compilation: 256 when enabled, 16 otherwise.

customProfile.description:
Settings for a user-defined Cargo profile. Custom profiles must declare `inherits` naming an existing (built-in or previously-defined) profile.

[Cargo documentation](https://doc.rust-lang.org/cargo/reference/profiles.html#custom-profiles)

inherits.description:
Name of the profile this one inherits from. Required for every custom profile. The four built-ins (`dev`, `release`, `test`, `bench`) are always valid; you may also inherit from another custom profile.

[Cargo documentation](https://doc.rust-lang.org/cargo/reference/profiles.html#custom-profiles)

rustflags.description: UNSTABLE: Extra compiler flags; requires -Z profile-rustflags.

codegen-backend.description: UNSTABLE: Compiler codegen backend; requires -Z codegen-backend.

trim-paths.description: UNSTABLE: Trim filesystem paths; requires -Z trim-paths.

hint-mostly-unused.description: UNSTABLE: Mark crates mostly unused; requires -Z profile-hint-mostly-unused.

dir-name.description: Removed: directory names follow the profile name.

debugAssertions.title: debug-assertions
debugAssertions.description:
Whether `debug_assert!` and related checks are compiled in.
Defaults: `true` for `dev`/`test`, `false` for `release`/`bench`.

[Cargo documentation](https://doc.rust-lang.org/cargo/reference/profiles.html#debug-assertions)

debugLevel.title: debug
debugLevel.description: Debug information: false/0/none disables it; 1/limited includes limited information; line-tables-only and line-directives-only are distinct modes; true/2/full includes full information.

limited.description: Limited debug information, equivalent to integer 1; distinct from line-tables-only.

line-directives-only.description: Line info directives only (useful for profilers).

line-tables-only.description: Line tables only — backtraces with file/line, no variables/types.

incremental.title: incremental
incremental.description:
Whether incremental compilation is enabled. May be overridden by the `CARGO_INCREMENTAL` env var or `build.incremental`.
Defaults: `true` for `dev`/`test`, `false` for `release`/`bench`.

[Cargo documentation](https://doc.rust-lang.org/cargo/reference/profiles.html#incremental)

lto.title: lto
lto.description:
Link-time optimization. `false` disables LTO with the local ThinLTO equivalent; `true`/`"fat"` performs fat LTO over the full dependency graph; `"thin"` is faster cross-crate ThinLTO; `"off"` disables LTO entirely (including local ThinLTO).
Default: `false`.

[Cargo documentation](https://doc.rust-lang.org/cargo/reference/profiles.html#lto)

enumValues: Thin LTO across crates — faster than fat, similar runtime gains.
Fat LTO across the whole dependency graph — slowest build, smallest/fastest binary.

fat.description: Fat LTO across the whole dependency graph — slowest build, smallest/fastest binary.

thin.description: Thin LTO across crates — faster than fat, similar runtime gains.

optLevel.title: opt-level
optLevel.description:
Optimization level. Integers `0`-`3` set increasing optimization; `"s"` optimizes for binary size; `"z"` optimizes for size while disabling loop vectorization.
Defaults: `0` for `dev`/`test`, `3` for `release`/`bench`.

[Cargo documentation](https://doc.rust-lang.org/cargo/reference/profiles.html#opt-level)

enumValues: Optimize for binary size, disabling loop vectorization.

z.description: Optimize for binary size, disabling loop vectorization.

overflowChecks.title: overflow-checks
overflowChecks.description:
Whether runtime integer overflow checks are emitted.
Defaults: `true` for `dev`/`test`, `false` for `release`/`bench`.

[Cargo documentation](https://doc.rust-lang.org/cargo/reference/profiles.html#overflow-checks)

packageOverrides.description:
Per-package profile overrides. Each key is a package name (or `"*"` for all dependencies, or a [`PackageId` spec](https://doc.rust-lang.org/cargo/reference/pkgid-spec.html) like `"serde@1.0.0"`).

[Cargo documentation](https://doc.rust-lang.org/cargo/reference/profiles.html#overrides)

panic.title: panic
panic.description: Panic strategy: unwind or abort. immediate-abort requires unstable panic-immediate-abort support. Ignored for test/bench profiles.

enumValues: Unwind the stack on panic, running destructors.
Terminate the process on panic without unwinding.

abort.description: Terminate the process on panic without unwinding.

unwind.description: Unwind the stack on panic, running destructors.

profilePackageSettings.description:
Per-package profile override. Cargo does not support `panic`, `lto`, or `rpath` here, and nested `build-override`/`package` are not allowed.

[Cargo documentation](https://doc.rust-lang.org/cargo/reference/profiles.html#overrides)

rustflags.description: UNSTABLE: Extra compiler flags; requires -Z profile-rustflags.

codegen-backend.description: UNSTABLE: Compiler codegen backend; requires -Z codegen-backend.

trim-paths.description: UNSTABLE: Trim filesystem paths; requires -Z trim-paths.

hint-mostly-unused.description: UNSTABLE: Mark crates mostly unused; requires -Z profile-hint-mostly-unused.

dir-name.description: Removed: directory names follow the profile name.

rpath.title: rpath
rpath.description:
Whether the compiler embeds an `rpath` into the final binary.
Default: `false`.

[Cargo documentation](https://doc.rust-lang.org/cargo/reference/profiles.html#rpath)

splitDebuginfo.title: split-debuginfo
splitDebuginfo.description:
Whether and how debug information is split out of the main executable.
Platform defaults: `"unpacked"` on macOS, `"packed"` on Windows MSVC, `"off"` elsewhere.

[Cargo documentation](https://doc.rust-lang.org/cargo/reference/profiles.html#split-debuginfo)

enumValues: Debug info embedded in the main artifact (or omitted on macOS).
Debug info packaged into a single separate file (`.dwp`/`.dSYM`/`.pdb`).
Debug info left in per-object files alongside the artifact.

off.description: Debug info embedded in the main artifact (or omitted on macOS).

packed.description: Debug info packaged into a single separate file (`.dwp`/`.dSYM`/`.pdb`).

unpacked.description: Debug info left in per-object files alongside the artifact.

strip.title: strip
strip.description:
Whether to strip symbols and/or debug info from the final binary. `true` is equivalent to `"symbols"`; `false` to `"none"`.
Default: `"none"`.

[Cargo documentation](https://doc.rust-lang.org/cargo/reference/profiles.html#strip)

enumValues: Strip both debug info and symbols.

symbols.description: Strip both debug info and symbols.

registries.title: [registries.*]
registries.description:
Additional registries and crates.io registry protocol settings.

[Cargo documentation](https://doc.rust-lang.org/cargo/reference/config.html#registries)

cratesIoRegistryConfig.description:
Settings for the official `crates-io` registry. Adds the `protocol` key (sparse vs. git index) on top of the shared registry properties. The default index URL is built into Cargo, so `index` is rarely set here.

[Cargo documentation](https://doc.rust-lang.org/cargo/reference/config.html#registriescrates-ioprotocol)

index.description:
URL of the registry index. Rarely set under `[registries.crates-io]` because Cargo ships the canonical URL. Environment: `CARGO_REGISTRIES_CRATES_IO_INDEX`.

[Cargo documentation](https://doc.rust-lang.org/cargo/reference/config.html#registriesnameindex)

token.description:
Authentication token for crates.io. Normally lives in `credentials.toml`, not `config.toml`. Environment: `CARGO_REGISTRIES_CRATES_IO_TOKEN`.

[Cargo documentation](https://doc.rust-lang.org/cargo/reference/config.html#registriesnametoken)

credential-provider.description:
Credential provider for crates.io. If unset, falls back to `registry.global-credential-providers`. Environment: `CARGO_REGISTRIES_CRATES_IO_CREDENTIAL_PROVIDER`.

[Cargo documentation](https://doc.rust-lang.org/cargo/reference/config.html#registriesnamecredential-provider)

protocol.description:
Protocol used to access crates.io. Only valid under `[registries.crates-io]`; user-defined registries advertise their protocol via the index URL itself (`sparse+https://...` or a git URL). Defaults to `"sparse"` since Cargo 1.70.

[Cargo documentation](https://doc.rust-lang.org/cargo/reference/config.html#registriescrates-ioprotocol)

enumValues: Clone the full git index from https://github.com/rust-lang/crates.io-index/. Slower for fresh resolves but mirrors the legacy behaviour.
Use the sparse HTTP index at https://index.crates.io/, fetching only the crates needed. Default since Cargo 1.70.

git.description: Clone the full git index from https://github.com/rust-lang/crates.io-index/. Slower for fresh resolves but mirrors the legacy behaviour.

sparse.description: Use the sparse HTTP index at https://index.crates.io/, fetching only the crates needed. Default since Cargo 1.70.

min-publish-age.description: Minimum publish age, for example "7 days" or "0". Requires Cargo 1.100+.

secret-key.description: UNSTABLE: Asymmetric credential secret key; requires -Z asymmetric-token. Store in credentials.toml.

secret-key-subject.description: UNSTABLE: Subject for asymmetric credentials; requires -Z asymmetric-token.

customRegistryConfig.description:
Settings for a user-defined registry (any name other than `crates-io`). `protocol` is omitted: non-crates.io registries select their protocol through the `index` URL scheme (`sparse+https://...` for sparse, plain URL for git).

[Cargo documentation](https://doc.rust-lang.org/cargo/reference/config.html#registriesname)

index.description:
URL of the registry index. For sparse registries use `sparse+https://...`; for git registries use a plain `https://...` URL. Environment: `CARGO_REGISTRIES_<NAME>_INDEX`.

[Cargo documentation](https://doc.rust-lang.org/cargo/reference/config.html#registriesnameindex)

token.description:
Authentication token for the registry. Normally lives in `credentials.toml`, not `config.toml`. Environment: `CARGO_REGISTRIES_<NAME>_TOKEN`.

[Cargo documentation](https://doc.rust-lang.org/cargo/reference/config.html#registriesnametoken)

credential-provider.description:
Credential provider for this registry. If unset, falls back to `registry.global-credential-providers`. Environment: `CARGO_REGISTRIES_<NAME>_CREDENTIAL_PROVIDER`.

[Cargo documentation](https://doc.rust-lang.org/cargo/reference/config.html#registriesnamecredential-provider)

min-publish-age.description: Minimum publish age, for example "7 days" or "0". Requires Cargo 1.100+.

secret-key.description: UNSTABLE: Asymmetric credential secret key; requires -Z asymmetric-token. Store in credentials.toml.

secret-key-subject.description: UNSTABLE: Subject for asymmetric credentials; requires -Z asymmetric-token.

registry.title: [registry]
registry.description:
Default registry and crates.io credential settings.

[Cargo documentation](https://doc.rust-lang.org/cargo/reference/config.html#registry)

index.description: REMOVED: registry.index is no longer accepted. Use registries.<name>.index or source configuration.

default.description:
Name of the registry (from the `registries` table) to use by default for registry commands like `cargo publish`. Can be overridden with `--registry`. Environment: `CARGO_REGISTRY_DEFAULT`.
https://doc.rust-lang.org/cargo/reference/config.html#registrydefault

credential-provider.description:
Credential provider for crates.io. If unset, falls back to `registry.global-credential-providers`. If the value matches a key in `[credential-alias]`, the alias is used. Environment: `CARGO_REGISTRY_CREDENTIAL_PROVIDER`.

[Cargo documentation](https://doc.rust-lang.org/cargo/reference/config.html#registrycredential-provider)

token.description:
Authentication token for crates.io. Should normally only appear in `credentials.toml`. Can be overridden with `--token`. Environment: `CARGO_REGISTRY_TOKEN`.

[Cargo documentation](https://doc.rust-lang.org/cargo/reference/config.html#registrytoken)

global-credential-providers.description:
Ordered list of global credential providers used when a registry does not configure its own. Order is significant: providers toward the END of the list have precedence. Path and arguments split on spaces; for paths/args containing spaces, define an alias in `[credential-alias]` and reference it here. Environment: `CARGO_REGISTRY_GLOBAL_CREDENTIAL_PROVIDERS`.

[Cargo documentation](https://doc.rust-lang.org/cargo/reference/config.html#registryglobal-credential-providers)

global-min-publish-age.description: Minimum publish age, for example "7 days" or "0". Requires Cargo 1.100+.

secret-key.description: UNSTABLE: Asymmetric credential secret key; requires -Z asymmetric-token. Store in credentials.toml.

secret-key-subject.description: UNSTABLE: Subject for asymmetric credentials; requires -Z asymmetric-token.

resolver.title: [resolver]
resolver.description:
Dependency resolver behavior for local development.

[Cargo documentation](https://doc.rust-lang.org/cargo/reference/config.html#resolver)

lockfile-path.description:
Path to the lockfile to use when resolving dependencies. Useful with read-only source directories. The path must end with `Cargo.lock`. Requires Cargo 1.97+. Environment: `CARGO_RESOLVER_LOCKFILE_PATH`.

[Cargo documentation](https://doc.rust-lang.org/cargo/reference/config.html#resolverlockfile-path)

incompatible-rust-versions.description:
How dependency versions with incompatible package.rust-version values are treated.
https://doc.rust-lang.org/cargo/reference/config.html#resolverincompatible-rust-versions Default is allow for resolver 1/2 and fallback for resolver 3.

enumValues: Treat rust-version-incompatible versions like any other version.
Only consider rust-version-incompatible versions if no compatible version matched.

allow.description: Treat rust-version-incompatible versions like any other version.

fallback.description: Only consider rust-version-incompatible versions if no compatible version matched.

incompatible-publish-age.description: How to handle versions younger than the minimum publish age. Requires Cargo 1.100+.

feature-unification.description: UNSTABLE: Feature unification scope; requires -Z feature-unification.

sources.title: [source.*]
sources.description:
Named registry source definitions and source replacement.

[Cargo documentation](https://doc.rust-lang.org/cargo/reference/config.html#source)

source.description: Source definition. At most one source location; crates-io can use its implicit location. Other sources require a location after merging. replace-with redirects the identified source.

replace-with.description: Replacement source name. The source location still identifies what is replaced.

local-registry.description:
Path to a local registry source.

[Cargo documentation](https://doc.rust-lang.org/cargo/reference/config.html#sourcenamelocal-registry)

git.description:
URL of a git repository source.

[Cargo documentation](https://doc.rust-lang.org/cargo/reference/config.html#sourcenamegit)

branch.description: Git reference selector. Cargo prefers branch, then tag, then rev when multiple are present; otherwise uses the default branch.

tag.description: Git reference selector. Cargo prefers branch, then tag, then rev when multiple are present; otherwise uses the default branch.

rev.description: Git reference selector. Cargo prefers branch, then tag, then rev when multiple are present; otherwise uses the default branch.

targets.title: [target.*]
targets.description:
Target-specific platform settings. Keys are target triples, cfg expressions, or custom target names.

[Cargo documentation](https://doc.rust-lang.org/cargo/reference/config.html#target)

propertyNames.description: Target triple (e.g. `x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu`), `cfg(...)` expression, or the filename stem of a custom target spec JSON file. Must be non-empty and start with a non-whitespace character.

linker.description:
Linker passed to rustc for this target.

[Cargo documentation](https://doc.rust-lang.org/cargo/reference/config.html#targettriplelinker)

runner.description:
Runner command used to execute target binaries.

[Cargo documentation](https://doc.rust-lang.org/cargo/reference/config.html#targettriplerunner)

rustflags.description:
Extra rustc flags for this target.

[Cargo documentation](https://doc.rust-lang.org/cargo/reference/config.html#targettriplerustflags)

rustdocflags.description:
Extra rustdoc flags for this target.

[Cargo documentation](https://doc.rust-lang.org/cargo/reference/config.html#targettriplerustdocflags)

target.title: target entry
target.description:
Settings applied when building for a single target. The owning key is a target triple (e.g. `x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu`), a `cfg(...)` expression, or a custom JSON target name. Recognised properties configure the linker, runner, and rustc/rustdoc flags; any additional key is treated as a `links` library override (build script metadata).

[Cargo documentation](https://doc.rust-lang.org/cargo/reference/config.html#target)

linker.description:
Linker passed to rustc for this target.

[Cargo documentation](https://doc.rust-lang.org/cargo/reference/config.html#targettriplelinker)

runner.description:
Runner command used to execute target binaries.

[Cargo documentation](https://doc.rust-lang.org/cargo/reference/config.html#targettriplerunner)

rustflags.description:
Extra rustc flags for this target.

[Cargo documentation](https://doc.rust-lang.org/cargo/reference/config.html#targettriplerustflags)

rustdocflags.description:
Extra rustdoc flags for this target.

[Cargo documentation](https://doc.rust-lang.org/cargo/reference/config.html#targettriplerustdocflags)

targetLinksOverride.title: links library override
targetLinksOverride.description:
Build script override for a target `links` library. When present, the build script for the named library is skipped and these values are used instead. Arbitrary keys beyond the recognised `rustc-*` set become opaque metadata exposed to dependents as `DEP_<links>_<KEY>` env vars.

[Cargo documentation](https://doc.rust-lang.org/cargo/reference/config.html#targettriplelinks)

rustc-link-lib.title: rustc-link-lib
rustc-link-lib.description: Libraries to link, equivalent to passing `-l <lib>` to `rustc`. Order is preserved and may affect symbol resolution.

rustc-link-search.title: rustc-link-search
rustc-link-search.description: Library search paths, equivalent to passing `-L <path>` to `rustc`. Searched in the listed order.

rustc-flags.title: rustc-flags
rustc-flags.description: Extra `rustc` flags. Whitespace-separated string; only `-l` and `-L` flags are accepted.

rustc-cfg.title: rustc-cfg
rustc-cfg.description: Custom `--cfg` flags enabled while compiling dependents of this links library. Order is preserved.

rustc-env.title: rustc-env
rustc-env.description: Environment variables exposed to `rustc` while compiling dependents of this links library.

rustc-cdylib-link-arg.title: rustc-cdylib-link-arg
rustc-cdylib-link-arg.description: Extra link args appended when building a `cdylib` that depends on this links library. Order is preserved (passed to the linker positionally).

docs.main:
Controls whether or not log messages are displayed by Cargo.

Mutually exclusive with `term.verbose` --- they cannot both be `true`. The `--quiet` CLI flag overrides and forces quiet output; `--verbose` overrides and disables it.

Default: `false`. Environment: `CARGO_TERM_QUIET`.

Controls whether or not extra detailed messages are displayed by Cargo.

Mutually exclusive with `term.quiet` --- they cannot both be `true`. The `--verbose` CLI flag overrides and forces verbose output; `--quiet` overrides and disables it.

Default: `false`. Environment: `CARGO_TERM_VERBOSE`.

Controls whether or not colored output is used in the terminal.

- `"auto"` --- automatically detect if color support is available.
- `"always"` --- always display colors.
- `"never"` --- never display colors.

Can be overridden with the `--color` CLI option. Default: `"auto"`. Environment: `CARGO_TERM_COLOR`.

hyperlinks.description:
Whether Cargo uses hyperlinks in terminal output. Auto-detected when unset.

[Cargo documentation](https://doc.rust-lang.org/cargo/reference/config.html#termhyperlinks)

docs.main:
Controls whether or not hyperlinks are used in the terminal.

When unset, Cargo auto-detects terminal support --- there is no static default. Environment: `CARGO_TERM_HYPERLINKS`.

unicode.description:
Whether Cargo can render non-ASCII Unicode characters. Auto-detected when unset.

[Cargo documentation](https://doc.rust-lang.org/cargo/reference/config.html#termunicode)

docs.main:
Controls whether output can be rendered using non-ASCII Unicode characters.

When unset, Cargo auto-detects terminal support --- there is no static default. Environment: `CARGO_TERM_UNICODE`.

when.description:
Whether Cargo shows a progress bar.

[Cargo documentation](https://doc.rust-lang.org/cargo/reference/config.html#termprogresswhen)

docs.main:
Controls whether or not the progress bar is shown in the terminal.

- `"auto"` --- intelligently guess whether to show the progress bar.
- `"always"` --- always show the progress bar.
- `"never"` --- never show the progress bar; `term.progress.width` then has no effect.

Default: `"auto"`. Environment: `CARGO_TERM_PROGRESS_WHEN`.

width.description: Progress width in columns (non-negative). Required when when = "always".

term-integration.description:
Whether Cargo reports progress to the terminal emulator (e.g. taskbar). Auto-detected when unset.

[Cargo documentation](https://doc.rust-lang.org/cargo/reference/config.html#termprogressterm-integration)

docs.main:
Reports progress to the terminal emulator for display in places like the taskbar.

When unset, Cargo auto-detects terminal support --- there is no static default. Environment: `CARGO_TERM_PROGRESS_TERM_INTEGRATION`.

title: cargo configuration
description:
Bundled Cargo configuration schema (auto-generated by cargo-schema-bundle from cargo-config.schema.json + sibling section schemas). Edit the split files, then re-run cargo-schema-bundle.
https://doc.rust-lang.org/cargo/reference/config.html

include.description:
Additional Cargo configuration files to include. Paths are relative to the including configuration file and must end with .toml.

[Cargo documentation](https://doc.rust-lang.org/cargo/reference/config.html#include)

paths.description:
Local package paths used as dependency overrides.

[Cargo documentation](https://doc.rust-lang.org/cargo/reference/config.html#paths)

target-applies-to-host.description: UNSTABLE: Apply target settings to host builds; requires -Z target-applies-to-host.

path-bases.description: UNSTABLE: Named path bases; requires path-bases support.

publish.description: UNSTABLE: Publish settings; timeout requires -Z publish-timeout.

host.description: UNSTABLE: Host platform overrides; requires -Z host-config and -Z target-applies-to-host.
